claim: The Luxembourg Moselle wine region runs ~42 km from Schengen to Wasserbillig along the German border, with limestone and clayey-marl soils.
quote: The Moselle Valley stretches for approximately 42 kilometers from Schengen to Wasserbillig

claim: Luxembourg has ~1,290 ha of vineyard under the Appellation Contrôlée Moselle Luxembourgeoise; Elbling has shrunk to ~4% of plantings.
quote: 1,290 hectares of vines are used to produce wine under the designation Appellation Contrôlée Moselle Luxembourgeoise

claim: Crémant de Luxembourg AOP, decreed in 1991, is the only sparkling wine outside France allowed to use 'Crémant'.
quote: Crémant de Luxembourg was decreed a designation in 1991 at the time the Appellation Contrôlée Crémant de Luxembourg was established

claim: Caves de Wellenstein (Domaines Vinsmoselle) is open for tasting Mon–Fri 9–17h, Sat & holidays 10–17h, with guided cellar visits ~60 min on demand (closed during September harvest).
quote: The team welcomes visitors from Monday to Friday from 9 a.m. - 5 p.m. and from 10 a.m – 5 p.m. on Saturdays and public holidays

claim: Caves de Wellenstein, founded 1930, is the largest Domaines Vinsmoselle site and the central shipping point for the cooperative covering 240 winegrowers.
quote: Founded in 1930, the Caves de Wellenstein is now the largest site of the Domaines Vinsmoselle, which includes 240 wineries

claim: Caves Bernard-Massard in Grevenmacher offers guided tours April–October daily except Monday, 10am–6pm; off-season by appointment.
quote: Guided tours and tasting sessions are available April-October daily except Monday from 10am-6pm

claim: Caves St Martin in Remich offers guided tours through ~1 km of limestone galleries at a constant 12°C, with Crémant tasting; reservations required 48h ahead.
quote: underground tunnels nearly a kilometre long that have been carved into solid limestone rock. The temperature in the tunnels is a constant, damp 12°C

claim: Domaine Sunnen-Hoffmann in Remerschen has farmed organically since 2000 and was the first Luxembourg-Moselle estate to do so; ~8.5 ha total.
quote: In 2001, Domaine Sunnen-Hoffmann became the first winery in the Luxembourgish Moselle Valley to grow its vines organically

claim: Domaine Henri Ruppert in Schengen is a hillside estate offering reservation-only tastings (~€14 for 4 wines) with panoramic views over the Luxembourg–Germany–France tri-border.
quote: Cellar visits are only available upon reservation

claim: Maison Viticole Schmit-Fohl in Ahn is a 7th-generation 14.5 ha estate that has been converting to organic since 2020 under brothers Nicolas and Mathieu.
quote: Nicolas and Mathieu took over the 14.5 hectares of the Estate in 2021 and have worked at converting the vineyards to organic

claim: Domaine Madame Aly Duhr in Ahn is a fifth-generation family winery with nearly 150 years of grape-growing tradition.
quote: fifth-generation family-owned winery with almost 150 years of grapegrowing and winemaking tradition in Ahn Luxembourg

claim: MS Princesse Marie-Astrid runs themed weekend cruises in 2026, including a 'Sunday Lunch' service Apr 19–Sep 20 and Saturday excursions to Saarburg (€32 round-trip).
quote: Sunday - The Sunday Lunch Runs: April 19 - September 20, 2026

claim: MS Princesse Marie-Astrid, built 2010 and 60 m long, capacity 500; the original was the boat where the 1985 Schengen Agreement was signed.
The Schengen Museum is open daily 10:00–18:00 (closed Nov 1, 2026); adult €5, child 7-17 €3; bus stop 'Schengen, Ennen am Doref'.
Musée A Possen in Bech-Kleinmacher is a folklore, wine and toy museum with €5 adult entry; opening hours subject to seasonal variation.
quote: Musée A Possen - Musée folklorique et viticole - Musée de jouets

claim: Riesling Open is held the 3rd weekend of September across Wormeldange, Ehnen, Ahn and Machtum, with free MS Princesse Marie-Astrid shuttle between villages on Sunday.
quote: The four wine villages of Wormeldange, Ehnen, Ahn and Machtum open their cellars together

claim: Caves Bernard-Massard, founded 1921 in Grevenmacher, is a Falstaff-listed traditional-method sparkling specialist with cellar visits and panoramic Moselle terrace.
Five Vinsmoselle cooperative cellars (Greiveldange, Grevenmacher, Remerschen, Stadtbredimus, Wellenstein) collectively work over 800 ha — about two-thirds of national vineyard area.
quote: The cooperatives in Greiveldange, Grevenmacher, Remerschen, Stadtbredimus and Wellenstein source their wines from over 800 hectares
